title: When the Church disappoints
hookLine: scandal and failure are real and grievous
tomorrow: so why did Peter stay when others walked away?

cards: A gentle word first: today touches abuse in the Church, without details.

Sometimes the headline is about your own: a name you recognize, a diocese you know, harm done by people meant to protect, and kept quiet for too long. What do you say? Scripture has words for this, and they aren't polite.
Through the prophet Ezekiel, God says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Woe to the shepherds of Israel, that fed themselves."

teach.h: THE LOST THEY DID NOT SEEK.
teach.b: Ezekiel goes on: the weak they did not strengthen, the lost they did not seek. Then God says he will seek the lost himself and bind up what was broken.

Pope Francis wrote a letter to the whole Church owning this wound. He called the abuse crimes, said the Church had not cared for the little ones and had abandoned them, and asked every Catholic for penance and prayer.
So the Church's own sources don't ask anyone to defend the indefensible, or to stop feeling it.
They hand over lament instead, the psalm's cry: "How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end?" Honest grief can stand right beside faith.
And if any of this is your own story: it was not your fault, and you deserve to be believed.
Tell someone you trust, or report it to the authorities. If you're in danger or thinking of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.

how: Catholic dioceses keep safe-environment programs and reporting lines, and parishes pray for survivors; Catholics can bring grief and anger to prayer in the psalms of lament.

games.q: what does “when the church disappoints” mean?
o: believing nothing bad could happen in a parish
proof that faith itself was never real at all
facing real failure in the Church with honest grief

p: named the crimes, asked for penance

s: the Church's own sources ask Catholics to keep quiet about abuse
Francis wrote to the whole Church naming the crimes and asking for penance and prayer.
Ezekiel's prophecy condemns shepherds who fed themselves
woe to the shepherds of Israel, that fed themselves.
a lector ends the reading by saying the end
the lector says the word of the Lord, and the people answer thanks be to God.

games.q: you want to pray about the news, but you're too angry to be polite with God. what does the psalm show?
o: you can ask God how long, angry and honest.
prayer has to stay calm, so wait until you cool off.
anger at God means the faith is already gone.
games.why: how long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end? the psalm brings the anger straight to God.

practice: Take a pen and write one honest sentence about a way the Church, or any people of faith, have let you or someone you love down. Don't soften it.
If you pray, you can read it to God the way the psalmist asked how long; if not, simply let it be said, and set the pen down.

wordCard.voice: When the Church disappoints. Facing real failure in the Church honestly, with grief that isn't hidden or explained away. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: how long, O Lord? the psalm's cry in the Vulgate (Psalm 12; 13 in most Bibles).

carryVoice: Keep this one: honest grief, the kind the psalms already make room for. That's the week.
